name: Gimme Truth! Documentary 2
brief: Project for my Film Production II class.  We were tasked to make a 2 minute documentary that was either 100% true or 100% false, based on the True/False film festival's 'Gimme Truth' competition.  We were assigned groups of 3 or 4, and it had to be related to a brand in some way or another.
description: My group decided to tell the fictional story of one of our members.  We had to get the video to be exactly 2 minutes, and the story kept being told in under 1:20, so I had to play with the pacing in the edit, combining different takes, as well as the B-roll another member collected one night.  I had a lot of fun playing with the soundscape to tell this story and faking the text exchange at the end.

name: Stock Footage Commercial
brief: Project for my Film Production II class.  We were tasked to make a 60 second commercial entirely out of stock footage, preferably without showing the specific brand or product until the end.  This was intended to show our editing abilities, using footage we didn't have to create ourselves.
description: (DISCLAIMER: This was a student project and so the use of the brand was permitted for educational purposes.  This was not an offical ad for the company.)  For this commercial, I chose to do a beauty company (and essentially picked one that fit the aesthetic I was trying to achieve).  I wanted to tell the story of how beauty routines are linked to social relationships for so many women, and the positive memories attached to them.  I chose to create this soft atmosphere with the pacing, soundscape, and voiceover to evoke nostalgia and tell a generational story.

name: Six-Mile Ordinary Commercial
brief: Project for my Film Production II class.  As an entire class we made a 60 second commercial for a local distillery, Six-Mile Ordinary.  We were all assigned individual roles and then had to create our own final edit of the footage.
description: My role on set was Director of Photography.  I created the shot list that was then executed when filming, where I either worked on main camera or collected b-roll (all of the moving shots).  This was the version I submitted in class, although I'm not super happy with all elements.  I struggled with finding royalty-free music that fit the atmosphere I was trying to create, and had some issues with the audio quality of the shots in the bar area.  To improve this project, I would get have the actors ADR some of the audio, and spend more time testing exploring my music options.

name: 10 Minute Documentary
brief: Project for my Film Production I class.  We had to make a short documentary (defined as 10 minutes or less) with a clear beginning, middle and end on a subject of our choosing.
description: (Note: This is the finished version for class, but not the actual finished version for this story.)  I chose to make my documentary about my hometown.  Specifically, its involvement in the Underground Railroad.  However, through my interviews I managed to get a lot of footage and information on this and similar topics, enough to potentially make a much longer documentary later on.  I spent multiple weekends interviewing people and getting B-roll, although there's a lot of information I left untouched due to tiem constraints.

name: Don't Do As Roman! Short Film
brief: Group project for my Film Production I class.  Everyone pitched a short film, which we voted for which ones we wanted to work on, and were assigned into groups from there.
description: My film wasn't chosen to be produced which meant I was not the director.  Instead I filled a variety of roles like Producer, Assistant Director, Camerawoman, etc.  The film wasn't my personal vision, and I would have approached the storytelling differently, however my job was to fulfill that of the director, which I feel I did effectively.  I also fell sick during the bulk of the filming days, and was only there for two of the final scenes.  As part of the group, however, we all got to make our own final edit, which is where I was able to really shine.  I created all the graphics myself in Photoshop and then used After Effects to incorporate them into the final edit.

name: Gimme Truth! Documentary
brief: Project for my Film Production I class.  We were tasked to make a 2 minute documentary that was either 100% true or 100% false, based on the True/False film festival's 'Gimme Truth' competition.
description: I used my friend as the subject for my documentary (or mockumentary in this case).  I wanted to make a subtitled film, so I recruited my friend who spoke Polish and made up the fact that she doesn't like pierogi.  I'd never made a documentary (mock or not) before, so I wanted to experiment with the traditional techniques of documentary (two different camera angles for interviews, somewhat related kitchen B-roll, etc).  It was filmed over the course of a few hours, and I had a lot of fun making it and getting to experiment with subtle ways to add humor (pacing the dumpling 'reveal', using the Wendy's sweet-n-sour sauce, etc), even if the Polish-to-English translation isn't quite there (I mostly made stuff up).  I actually submitted the film to the 2026 edition of Gimme Truth! and made it in, so it was shown at the True/False film festival.

name: Visual Poem
brief: Project for my Intro to Digital Storytelling class.  We had to evoke a specific mood through our imagery and soundscape to match the poem we used as voiceover.  We also had to include either experimental footage or symbolic/metaphoric imagery.
description: I was inspired by the poem 'The Ambition Bird' by Anne Sexton in both pacing and mood, but because we were expected to own the rights to everything we used, I wrote my own poem for the voiceover.  I wanted to capture the feeling of late-night anxiety, where you might not feel any of this during the morning when you wake up, but because you can't fall asleep, it's all you can think about.  Whether it's stressing over the next day or the awkward thing you did five years ago, your thoughts can't stop spiraling about everything you can't control.  I also wanted to play with the idea of reflections and how they are inherently skewed (literally and metaphorically), with this idea that the speaker of poem is 'reflecting' on her day, but also that we only see ourselves in reflections, and how rarely they match with reality.

name: Light and Composition Video
brief: Project for my Intro to Digital Storytelling class.  We essentially were told to make our 'reel' by practicing camera and editing techniques, like camera tilts and pans, graphic matching, natural wipes, as well as making everything look pretty with our composition and lighting.
description: I essentially spent an entire weekend wandering around campus (and one evening at a nearby park) and filming anything I thought was pretty, or interesting, including myself in a lot of the shots as 'the subject'.  I then spent a lot of time editing those shots together to find 'happy accidents' with continuity, or some planned ones (the transition between the couches, for instance), as well as finding the perfect song that I could match the beats to the visuals.

name: Light and Composition Video Re-edit to 1minute
brief: As extra editing practice, my professor challenged us to re-edit our Light and Composition Video to be one minute or less.
description: This was a bit more of a struggle because there were a lot of shots I loved and didn't necessarily have a way to transition between them, especially once I got rid of sequences I wasn't as attached to.

name: Photostory
brief: Project for my Intro to Digital Storytelling class.  We were told to tell a story using only still images and a complete soundscape.  The purpose of this was to practice composition and sound editing.
description: This was the first project I got to do for this class, and I'm quite proud of it.  I love comedy, and was very proud of myself for coming up with this concept.  There are a few tweaks I would make if I were to redo this project with my current experience, but for the most part, I would say it still holds up really well.

name: Animation Practice
brief: Project for my IT Media Design class.  We had to make a 15 second animated ad for the fictional company 'RetroWeird Software'.  All imagery was either provided my professor or created by me.  The logo was created by me for a previous assignment.
description: This was my first time using After Effects, but not my first time key-framing.  It was fun getting to experiment with different transitions in AfterEffects.  It gave me a familiarity with the software that I was able to use for other classes afterwards.

name: Welcome Video for Incoming 7th Graders
brief: One of my earliest video editing projects.  I was tasked with editing the footage collected by the class to make one complete video to be showed when the sixth graders came to visit/tour the middle school.
description: I recently dug up this video from 7th grade.  I remember being so proud that my teacher wanted me specifically to be the one to do the final editing, because she knew I was responsible and skilled enough.  I had previously completed two other editing projects in 6th and 7th grade (a horror movie trailer and a lyric video for a song of my choice), so I was already familiar with Adobe Premiere, and doing this I got to learn a bunch of other new things as well.
